page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d3c.3xlarge is a big data instance family configuration deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a baseline clock speed of 2.9 GHz, delivering 14 dedicated vCPUs. System memory is sized at 56.0 GB, providing an even allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. Networking infrastructure is provisioned with an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the server includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

A primary architectural characteristic of the ecs.d3c.3xlarge is its bundled local storage array, offering 13743 GB across local hard disk drives (HDD). By using dense mechanical storage media rather than solid-state drives, the instance maximizes capacity per compute node while accepting the mechanical latency tradeoffs inherent to HDDs. The server includes no discrete GPU hardware acceleration.

The combination of 14 dedicated compute cores, a standard 1:4 memory ratio, and an expansive 13.7 TB local HDD footprint targets data-intensive throughput applications. It is suited for distributed big data frameworks such as Apache Hadoop and MapReduce, high-capacity data ingestion pipelines, sequential log processing, and batch ETL processing where local disk volume takes precedence over random-access IOPS performance.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d3c.3xlarge is a dedicated big data server within the d3c family, operating on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 14 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor at 2.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, alongside 56.0 GB of RAM, yielding 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is distinguished by 13743 GB of bundled local HDD storage and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Without discrete GPU accelerators, the server trades the low-latency random access of flash storage for high-density, economical local disk volume. This storage-heavy profile fits distributed big data systems, batch ETL processing, MapReduce analytics, and sequential log storage environments requiring large local capacity coupled with balanced multi-core CPU capacity.
